current_values: ["Churchill became prime minister in May 1940 and formed a wartime coalition. His Conservative affiliation should not be mistaken for the composition of that all-party administration. Britain’s war effort depended on military operations and cooperation with allies; the government continued to operate through parliamentary institutions. George VI remained monarch throughout the war. The leadership records preserve the change to Attlee in 1945 rather than assigning one prime minister to the entire transition year.","Attlee’s Labour government followed the 1945 election. Its programme expanded public services and nationalised important industries. The National Health Service and national insurance legislation were central to postwar reconstruction. Overseas, the government presided over independence for India and Pakistan and the end of British rule in other territories. These were changes in imperial relationships, not grounds for treating every formerly governed territory as a part of the United Kingdom’s domestic census population."]
